title: Cartesian proper changes of ambient scheme in the explicit graph comparison
statement: Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, and use the ordinary unbounded small-etale module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Fix $f:X\to Y$, a compactification $c$ and two proper/open/proper presentations $s=(a_s,e_s,p_s)$ and $t=(a_t,e_t,p_t)$ [def-pur-etale-graph-presentation-maps]. Let $r:P_t\to P_s$ be proper and $q:U_t\to U_s$ such that the square with top $e_t$, bottom $e_s$, left $q$ and right $r$ is Cartesian [def-pc-fibre-product], $q a_t=a_s$, and $p_s r=p_t$. Write $R_g=Rg_*$ and $J_j=Dj_!$, with the canonical direct-image compositors [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. Define $L:F_s\to F_t$ by inserting $R_{a_s}\cong R_{a_t}R_q$, applying the Cartesian proper/open interchange $J_{e_s}R_q\to R_rJ_{e_t}$ [lem-pur-etale-proper-open-exchange-cube], and composing $R_{p_s}R_r\cong R_{p_t}$. Then the specified graph comparisons [lem-sf-etale-locally-closed-graph-model] satisfy $L B_{s,c}=B_{t,c}$. This statement involves no shrinking of the supporting open and requires no quasi-compactness.

proof.text: Construct the product map and its two Cartesian supporting-neighborhood squares by explicit pullback lifts. Their proved graph equations give the first and second transport isomorphisms.
The first-side and second-side pasting equations compare the two side factors against these transports.
The intersection pasting equation identifies the two middle words against the same transports. The graph model supplies the four graph properness proofs.

Expand B_s and B_t into first side, middle, inverse second side. Postcompose with the new second side. Replace L followed by that side using the second-side equation, cancel the old second side, substitute the middle equation and then the first-side equation. Cancel the new second side to obtain exactly B_s L = B_t.

theorem etaleGraphComparisonFromOpen_properAmbient
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A]
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Y} (c : Compactification f)
    (s t : EtaleGraphPresentation f) (pr : t.P ⟶ s.P) [IsProper pr]
    (q : t.U ⟶ s.U) (sq : IsPullback q t.e s.e pr)
    (hz : t.a ≫ q = s.a) (hp : pr ≫ s.p = t.p) :
    etaleGraphComparisonFromOpen A c s ≪≫
        Functor.isoWhiskerRight
          (rightDerivedLowerStarCompOfEq (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) t.a q s.a hz).symm _ ≪≫
        Functor.associator _ _ _ ≪≫
        Functor.isoWhiskerLeft _ ((Functor.associator _ _ _).symm ≪≫
          Functor.isoWhiskerRight (openImmersionLowerShriekLowerStarExchangeIso A sq) _ ≪≫
          Functor.associator _ _ _ ≪≫
          Functor.isoWhiskerLeft _
            (rightDerivedLowerStarCompOfEq (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) pr s.p t.p hp)) =
      etaleGraphComparisonFromOpen A c t

old_proof.text:
in the products `s.P ×_Y c.Z` and `t.P ×_Y c.Z`, the map induced by `pr`
is proper. The supporting neighborhood for `t` is the inverse image of the one
for `s` by the supplied Cartesian square. The neighborhood for `c` and their
intersection are also related by Cartesian proper maps. Their proper graph lifts
are compatible with these maps by the pullback projection equations and `hz`.
For each supporting neighborhood, expand the side word of the graph comparison.
Vertical pasting of the normalized proper/open exchange identifies this side word
with the old side word followed by the proper-projection exchange and direct-image
compositor. For the intersection word, apply vertical pasting to the graph triangle
above the proper-projection square and horizontal pasting to the two open inclusions.
Naturality interchanges the two exchange factors and gives the same projection
exchange at both ends. Substitute these equations in `B₂⁻¹ R(B₁₂) B₁`.
The two occurrences of the intersection projection exchange cancel. The remaining
side factor is precisely the displayed compositor--Cartesian-exchange word.
Associativity of the canonical direct-image and open compositors supplies the
parenthesizations shown below. The argument also applies to empty schemes and to
identity maps; it requires no quasi-compactness of either supporting open.
